newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian oil talks in limbo over natgas dispute.
newsitem.headline: Colombian oil talks in limbo over natgas dispute.

text.p: Collective contract talks between Colombia's main oil workers' union and state-run oil company Ecopetrol hung in limbo again Tuesday after renewed disagreement over natural gas operations.

Ecopetrol favors the creation of an independent company, jointly financed by the state and private sector, to handle gas production and distribution. But the 7,000-strong USO union rejects the proposal arguing that the gas company, to be known as Ecogas, should be a subsidiary of Ecopetrol.
Negotiations were broken off late Monday pending a congressional debate on Ecogas. That session, originally scheduled for Tuesday, has been postponed until Wednesday morning.
USO leader Hernando Hernandez said the future of natural gas operations was a "fundamental issue" in the collective contract talks, which began in earnest in early January.

He repeated previous threats that failure to reach agreement on the collective contract, which would remain in force for the next two years, could lead to a strike but did not say when this could begin.

"The question of Ecogas is fundamental. We consider making Ecogas an independent company is a negative step and could lead to the eventual break-up of Ecopetrol," Hernandez told Reuters in a phone interview.
"Without agreement on Ecogas there will be no collective contract deal and there would be a strike," he added.
An Ecopetrol spokesman said the creation of Ecogas as an independent company would relieve Ecopetrol of the burden of administering and financing natural gas operations.

"As an autonomous entity, Ecogas would have its own policies, its own budget and its own administration. As a mixed company it could also have private capital as well as state funds," the spokesman said. He described contract negotiations as "positive" but was unable to say when they might restart.

Over the last week, Ecopetrol and the USO overcame another obstacle in talks and agreed about 380 new workers would be contracted. No discussion has yet taken place over wage demands. Ecopetrol is offering an 18 percent pay hike while the USO is calling for a 28 percent rise.
Natural gas output averaged 444 million cubic feet per day last year and is forecast to increase to 517 million cubic feet per day this year. Most is used to drive thermo-electric power stations.
